sections.title: Getting started
items: Add your email account

Settings (⚙ or Ctrl+,) → Accounts → “＋ Add an account”.
• Choose the provider: the IMAP/SMTP servers fill in by themselves (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, iCloud, OVH, Infomaniak…). Other provider: enter the servers and ports by hand.
• Click “Test the connection” (IMAP + SMTP) then “Save”. The first synchronization starts right away.
• Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud: create an “app password” in the account's security settings and use it instead of your usual password — or, for Gmail and Outlook, choose the “OAuth” provider (see “Google / Microsoft sign-in”).
• Several accounts: add them all; the side panel shows one colored circle per account and the unified inbox merges them.
Google / Microsoft sign-in (OAuth, no password)

Settings → Accounts → provider “Gmail — Google sign-in (OAuth)” or “Outlook / Microsoft 365 — Microsoft sign-in (OAuth)”.
• MintMail cannot create these credentials for you: Google and Microsoft require it to be you, signed in to your account (NEVER give your credentials to a program or an assistant for this). On the first click on “Sign in”, a wizard guides you through 2 to 4 steps; each “Open ↗” button opens the right console page. Google: project “MintMail”, “Google Calendar API” enabled, “External” consent screen with the scopes https://mail.google.com/ and calendar.events, yourself as a test user, then “Publish”; credentials of type “Desktop app”. Microsoft: app registration as a “public client” with the URI http://localhost.
• Do it ONCE: the credentials you enter sync to your other machines (P2P sync).
• Several computers or a team: a file /etc/mintmail/oauth-clients.json of the form {"google": {"client_id": "…", "client_secret": "…"}} is used by every user of the machine, with no typing at all (an example is installed in /usr/share/doc/mintmail/oauth-clients.json.example; the package can also bundle it).
• For mail only, without creating anything at Google: choose the regular Gmail provider with an “app password” (Google account → Security → 2-step verification → app passwords): 1 minute, but no calendar.
• “Sign in” opens the provider's page in your browser; MintMail never sees your password. It keeps a token that you can revoke at any time from your Google or Microsoft account, stored like a password (keyring) and synced with your other machines.
• “Reconnect” renews the token if the provider revoked it.
• Google, important: while the consent screen is in “Testing” mode, Google makes the token EXPIRE after 7 days (you have to reconnect). For lasting personal use, switch the app to “In production” in the Google Cloud console: an “unverified app” screen appears once, to be accepted (up to 100 users, no verification needed).
Demo mode
With no account configured, MintMail shows sample messages so you can try the interface (folders, AI, composing). Adding a real account automatically replaces the demo.
Getting around the window

• Side panel: smart views (Inbox, Unread, Favorites, Pinned, Snoozed, Drafts), accounts and their folders, saved searches, and the machine-sync indicator (⇄) at the bottom.
• Message list in the middle, reader on the right. The dividers can be dragged with the mouse and the position is remembered.
• One click always opens the message. Selection mode (X key or button) shows checkboxes to act on several messages.
• ☰ menu: command palette, settings (also in a separate window), light / dark, mark all as read, error log, about.
• Narrow window: the side panel collapses and the reader takes the full width (Back button). F11: full screen.
List and reader layout

Settings → Gestures & layout: columns (list on the left, reader on the right), list on top / reader at the bottom, or list only. The \ key quickly switches between columns and list only. The side panel can be collapsed to an icon rail.

sections.title: Read and organize
items: The message list

Each row shows the sender, the subject, a preview (or the ✨ AI summary if there is one), the time, a colored priority bar (red: important or suspicious, blue: unread) and badges (attachment, favorite, pin, number of messages in a conversation). The list loads page by page and continuously: scroll down to show older messages (all the way to the oldest on the server).
Conversations

Messages of the same thread are grouped into ONE row with the number of messages. Opening the row shows the latest message; “Conversation · N other messages” above the body lists the earlier ones (click to read them). Archiving, deleting, marking, snoozing or filing a conversation applies to all its messages in the same folder. Opening a conversation marks it as read.
To turn off: Settings → Gestures & layout → “Group into conversations”. Search results stay flat.
Categories
In the inbox, the All / People / Notifications / Newsletters chips filter by sender type (detected automatically: mail from real people, service notifications, newsletters and promotions).
Your mailbox folders

All IMAP folders of each account are visible in the side panel (collapsible tree, unread counts). • Click a folder to browse it; the “older messages” button loads further back in the history.
• Move: V key, right-click menu or ☰, palette (“Move to…”), or the AI.
• Create, rename, delete a folder or subfolder: right-click a folder or an account.
• Special folders (Sent, Drafts, Archive, Spam, Trash) are recognized whatever the server's language.
Favorites, pins, snoozes, follow-ups

• Favorite (S): star synced with the server. Pin (P): keeps the message at the top of the list; it is ALSO stored on the mailbox (IMAP keyword), so your other computers see it at their next sync. Some servers (Gmail, Outlook.com) refuse this keyword: MintMail checks at the first try and warns you, and the pin then stays on this computer only. Palette → “Send my pins to the mailbox” sends the ones made before 1.13.2.
• Snooze (H = tomorrow 8:00, or right-click → Snooze): the message disappears and comes back to the top of the inbox at the chosen time (later today, tomorrow, this weekend, Monday, next week…).
• “Remind me if no reply” (reader ⋯ menu or right-click): MintMail warns you if the recipient has not replied after 3 days.
Search

Ctrl+F or /: search is instant on the subject, sender, recipients and body of downloaded messages.
Combinable operators: from:marie · is:unread · is:starred · has:attachment (e.g. “from:marie invoice is:unread”).
• “🔎 Search the server too” (under the search, or palette) queries the whole server, even messages never downloaded, and adds the results to the list.
• Natural-language search: start with “?” (e.g. “? unread mails from Marie this week”) — the AI turns your sentence into criteria.
• “Save the search” turns it into a permanent view in the side panel.
Actions on several messages
Selection mode (X) → tick or Ctrl+A, then archive (E), delete, mark, move (V), spam (!)… A bulk action bar appears. Actions are instant; an “Undo” banner stays available for a few seconds.
Swipe gestures

Drag a row with the mouse, touchpad or finger. By default: right = archive, long right = delete, left = snooze, long left = read/unread. Customizable in Settings → Gestures & layout (archive, delete, snooze, read, favorite, pin, spam, block, nothing) plus reversing the direction for the touchpad.

sections.title: Today, tasks and time slots
items: “Today” page (T key)

T key, ☰ menu → Today, or the palette. A single window to start your day:
• 📅 Today's calendar (Google Calendar, if enabled: Settings → Calendar). Option: Settings → Appearance → “Open the Today page at launch”.
• ⚡ To handle first: your UNREAD messages that AI sorting judges important (click = opens the message). Without AI, sorting is limited to simple clues.
• ☑ Open tasks, overdue first (tick to finish, ✉ to open the original message) and a field to add one.
• ⏳ Awaiting a reply: your scheduled follow-ups (“Remind me if no reply”).
• ✨ Draft replies prepared by the AI, to review (see below).
Tasks and due dates

• Create: right-click a message → “✔ Add to tasks…”, or “✨ Add the N detected task(s)” (those found by the AI analysis of the message), or palette → “New task…”, or the field on the Today page.
• The due date is read from the text. For now only French wording is understood — “demain” (tomorrow), “après-demain” (the day after), “avant vendredi” (before Friday), “ce vendredi”, “le 15/11”, “avant le 20 novembre”, “dans 3 jours” (in 3 days), “dans 2 semaines”, “la semaine prochaine” (next week), “fin de semaine” (end of the week), “fin du mois” (end of the month), “le 20” — plus numeric dates in any language (15/11, 15/11/2026). English phrases (“tomorrow”, “next Friday”) are not read yet. A day name means its next occurrence (today excluded, except “ce lundi”). No date found: the task has no due date.
• A task already added for the same message is never duplicated. Tasks sync between your machines (the most recent change wins).
Suggest time slots (from Google Calendar)

Right-click a message → “📅 Suggest time slots (calendar)” → 30 min / 1 h / 1 h 30. MintMail reads your calendar, finds 3 free slots on DIFFERENT working days and opens the reply with the text “I suggest the following time slots: …” for you to review and send.
Fixed rules: Monday–Friday, 9:00 to 17:30, starting 2 hours from now, over the next 15 days; “busy” events (including all-day ones) block, events marked “free” do not. The text follows the interface language. Requires Google Calendar to be enabled (Settings → Calendar); the option does not appear otherwise.
Draft replies prepared by the AI (optional)

Settings → AI → “Prepare draft replies (important messages)” (off by default).
• When a message arrives that the AI judges important, from a “person”, and that expects a reply (less than 3 days old), MintMail prepares a draft in Drafts (3 per pass at most). It is NEVER sent: you open it, review it, fix it, then you send.
• The draft imitates your style from a few of your sent messages: those excerpts are therefore sent to the AI provider (never with Ollama).
• The AI is instructed not to invent anything: any missing information is marked [TO COMPLETE: …] — review before sending, a model can be wrong.
• Prepared drafts also appear on the Today page (T key).

sections.title: Right-click, palette and shortcuts
items: Right-click menu on a message

• Reply, Reply all, Forward, ✨ Reply with AI.
• Archive, Delete, Mark read/unread, Favorite, Pin, Snooze, Move to a folder.
• Report as spam, Mark the sender as spam, Block the sender, See all its messages, Add to contacts, Unsubscribe (if the message offers it).
• ✨ AI section: File into the suggested folder (or “your habits”, or “Suggest a folder…”), Sort all messages from the sender, Sort my inbox, Always file this sender in this folder (rule), Reply with AI ▸ (suitable, accept, decline politely, ask for details, other time slot, formal tone, friendly tone, very short), Summarize the conversation, Summarize / analyze, Translate, Add to calendar (if an appointment is detected), Ask the assistant about this message.
If AI is not enabled, the section offers “Turn on AI”.
Reader bar

Reply, Reply all, Forward, Archive, Delete, ✨ Reply with AI, Spam ▾ and Block ▾ (this message, the address or the whole domain — with the actual address written in the choice), Move, Snooze, Favorite, Pin, and the ⋯ menu (read/unread, spam, blocking, unblock, follow-up reminder, etc.).
Command palette (Ctrl+K)

Type a few letters to find an action: reply, archive, move to a folder, spam / block the sender or their domain, unsubscribe, summarize, translate, open contacts or identities, calendar and new event, outbox, search the server, change view, style, layout, display… Enter runs, Esc closes.
All keyboard shortcuts
@SHORTCUTS@

sections.title: Compose and send
items: New message, reply, forward

C or Ctrl+N: new message. R / A / F: reply, reply all, forward (the quoted message is included). Addresses autocomplete from your address book and recent correspondents; Cc and Bcc show on demand. Closing the compose window with content offers to save a draft (found in Drafts).
Quick reply

Under each message: four ready-made replies (“Thanks!”, “OK, received 👍”…) and a “Quick reply…” field that sends a short reply without opening the compose window. The ✨ button expands your sentence into a full reply with the AI.
HTML signatures
Settings → Signatures: one signature per account (formatting, links, images), live preview. It is inserted automatically; changing the account in the “From” field changes the signature.
Sending identities (aliases)

Settings → Sending identities: add an extra address (alias) tied to an account, with its display name and signature. It appears in the “From” field of the compose window (“· alias”). When a received message was addressed to an alias, the reply automatically goes out from that alias. The account's server must allow the alias.
Reply templates
Settings → Reply templates: ready-to-insert texts (acknowledgement, meeting proposal…). They sync between your machines.
Undo send and scheduled send

• After “Send”, an “Undo” banner stays visible for a few seconds (3 to 30 s, Settings → Appearance).
• “Send later” (clock): choose this evening, tomorrow, Monday or a specific date.
• Scheduled messages go out even with the window closed: a user timer (mintmail-outbox) runs “mintmail --send-due” every minute. If it is not active yet in your session: systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now mintmail-outbox.timer.
• A double send is impossible (atomic reservation between the window and the timer).
• Palette → “Outbox”: see waiting or scheduled messages, “Send now” or “Cancel sending”.
Attachments when sending
Paperclip button, or drag files from your file manager onto the compose window (attachment area). The total is shown; above 20 MB it turns red: most servers refuse more than 20-25 MB.
✨ Writing help

“✨ AI” menu in the compose window: write from an idea, improve the text, fix spelling, shorten, expand, more formal tone, friendlier tone, translate, suggest a subject. The operation applies to the selection, otherwise to all your text (signature and quote excluded). Always review before sending.

sections.title: Artificial intelligence
items: Turn on the AI and choose the provider

Settings → ✨ Artificial intelligence. The AI is off by default.
• NVIDIA (cloud): paste your API key (nvapi-…), it is stored in the system keyring.
• Ollama (local): everything stays on your machine, no key. Install Ollama, run “ollama serve” and download a model (“ollama pull llama3.2”), then click “Detect installed models”.
• Other OpenAI-compatible service: address (https://… ; http:// only on this machine or the local network), model, optional key.
“Test the connection” checks everything. The provider, address and model sync between your machines (the key too, encrypted).
Privacy

Once the AI is on, the text of the processed messages is sent to the chosen provider (never with Ollama). “Privacy” setting: full text (best results) or minimal (first 500 characters). Results are kept in a local cache; “Clear the AI cache” erases them. The AI NEVER does anything without your approval: it proposes, you confirm.
Summary of each message

When you open a message, a ✨ SUMMARY box shows: a one-sentence synthesis, the key points, the tasks to do, the URGENT / low importance indication, and a ⚠ warning if the message looks like phishing. Without AI, a simple local summary is shown. “Analyze each message when opened” switch in the settings; otherwise, right-click → Summarize / analyze. No button bar: all actions are in the right-click menu.
Assistant (Ctrl+J)

A conversational panel able to ACT on your mailbox. Examples:
• “Summarize my mailbox” · “Which messages are urgent?”
• “Sort my latest emails into folders”
• “Create a folder called Invoices and file my invoices in it”
• “Archive newsletters I have already read” · “Mark promotional emails as spam”
• “Block the domain example.com” · “Create a rule for GitHub notifications”
• “Write a polite follow-up to Marie” · “Open the AI settings”
The assistant shows an action plan (“12 messages will be archived”…). You approve line by line or “Run all”. Possible actions: archive, delete, spam, read/unread, favorite, pin, snooze, move (the folder is created if missing), sort, create a folder, create a rule, block a sender, write, open a settings page, summarize.
AI sorting into folders

• In the assistant: “sort my emails”; or right-click → ✨ Sort all messages from the sender / Sort my inbox.
• The AI proposes a folder per message: an existing folder first, otherwise a short new name (6 new folders at most). It follows your filing habits.
• Nothing is moved or created before your approval (line by line or in bulk). Missing folders are created on the server when you approve.
• For a single message: ✨ File under “…” (suggested by the analysis, or “your habits”), or “Suggest a folder…”.
Your filing habits

When you file messages by hand into a folder, MintMail remembers “sender → folder” (locally only). From the 2nd time it suggests that folder (“your habits”); at the 3rd it offers to create an automatic rule. Settings → AI → “Forget my filing habits” erases everything.
Automatic sorting and “In brief”

• Sorting: new messages get a priority (colored bar, “Important” badge) and suspicious ones are flagged “Suspicious”.
• “In brief”: at the top of the inbox, a summary of what matters today. Each feature has its own switch in the AI settings.
Translation, questions, calendar

Right-click → Translate this message (into the language you set). Assistant or “?”: ask a question about the open message. If the AI detects an appointment: “Add to calendar” (see “Invitations and calendar”).
Language and tone
Settings → AI: AI language (French, English, Dutch, German, Spanish) and writing tone (neutral, formal, friendly).
Known limits

Models can be wrong: check the summaries, sorting and drafts. A small local model is slower and less accurate than a large cloud model. A network or key error is shown in plain words, without blocking the rest of MintMail.

sections.title: Spam, blocking, rules, unsubscribing
items: Spam and blocking

• Report as spam (!): moves the message to Spam.
• Spam ▾ / Block ▾ (reader) or right-click menu: choose the message alone, the sender's address, or the whole domain (@example.com). All the messages concerned are moved right away, and the next ones too (spam → Spam, blocked → Trash).
• B key: Block menu. Unblock: reader ⋯ menu or Settings → Filters & blocking. An Undo banner stays available.
• The lists (blocked, spam) are managed in Settings → Filters & blocking and sync between your machines.
Automatic rules

Settings → Filters & blocking → Rules: “If the sender / subject / recipient contains … then” archive, delete, spam, mark read, favorite, pin, or file into the folder … They apply to new messages (and “Apply now” to the inbox). A rule can also come from the right-click menu (“Always file…”) or from the assistant.
Unsubscribe

When a message contains an unsubscribe link (newsletters), the “Unsubscribe” button appears under the header, and the command exists in the right-click menu and the palette. • One-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058): MintMail sends the request directly, securely (HTTPS), after your confirmation. • Otherwise by email: the unsubscribe message is sent for you. • Otherwise the service's page opens in the browser. Afterwards, MintMail offers “Mark as spam” if messages still arrive.
Remote images and phishing

Remote images (tracking pixels) are blocked by default: “Remote images blocked” banner → Show, or the global setting in Appearance. The HTML of messages is cleaned (no scripts). Suspicious messages are flagged.

sections.title: Attachments, invitations, contacts, calendar
items: Received attachments

Under the header: one chip per file (thumbnail for images, name, size).
• Click: built-in preview of images and text files (txt, csv, json, md, log…), otherwise opens with the default application (PDF, Office…).
• Right-click: Open, Preview, Save as…, Copy path.
• “⬇ Save all” (2 files or more) copies everything into a folder without overwriting anything.
• Dragging a chip to the file manager or the desktop copies the file.
• Safety: programs and scripts (.exe, .sh, .desktop, .AppImage…) are never opened from MintMail (save only); HTML, SVG and macro-enabled Office files ask for confirmation.
Invitations

A message containing an invitation (.ics file) shows a 📅 box with the title, date and place:
• Accept / Maybe / Decline send the iCalendar reply to the organizer (understood by Outlook, Google, Apple…), from the address that received the invitation.
• “Add to calendar”: sent to Google Calendar if enabled (no duplicate if you click twice), otherwise to your CalDAV calendar, otherwise the .ics opens in your system calendar.
• With Google Calendar enabled, MintMail checks on opening whether the slot is free: “✔ You are free” or “⚠ Conflict with … (14:00–15:00)”.
An event cancellation is flagged.
Contacts

Settings → Contacts: cards (name, email, phone, company, notes), search, vCard (.vcf) import and export. Manual cards sync between your machines; correspondents picked up automatically from your messages (“auto”) feed address completion. Right-click a message → Add to contacts.
Google Calendar (Gmail)

Settings → Calendar (Google / CalDAV) → Google Calendar section. Setup, only once:
1. Connect your Gmail account with the “OAuth” provider (Settings → Accounts).
2. Google Cloud console (same project as for Gmail) → APIs & Services → Library → “Google Calendar API” → Enable.
3. “Authorize Google Calendar”: a Google page opens and the “calendar.events” permission is ADDED to the Gmail one; then turn on the “Use Google Calendar” switch and click “Test”.
What it brings:
• Accepted invitations and appointments detected by the AI (“Add to calendar”) go straight into Google Calendar, with no duplicates.
• Palette (Ctrl+K) → “Calendar: upcoming appointments”: your next 14 days; “New event…” button to create one (title, date, time, duration, place).
• When opening an invitation, a conflict warning or confirmation that you are free at that time.
If “calendar authorization missing” appears: redo step 3. If “the Google Calendar API is not enabled”: redo step 2. Token expired after 7 days: see the note about “Testing” mode in “Google / Microsoft sign-in”. The setting syncs between your machines.
CalDAV calendar (other calendar)

Settings → Calendar (Google / CalDAV), CalDAV section: calendar address (Nextcloud, Radicale, Fastmail, iCloud…), username, password, “Test” button. HTTPS required (HTTP only on the local network). Used only if Google Calendar is turned off; MintMail adds events to it, it does not read this calendar.

sections.title: Sync between your machines
items: How it works

MintMail automatically syncs your settings between your computers, with no server or account: discovery on the local network, encrypted and authenticated exchange. Synced: accounts (with passwords or OAuth tokens), signatures, AI (provider, model, key), reply templates, rules, blocks and spam, saved searches, sending identities, contacts, appearance, gestures, conversations, CalDAV. Not synced: the mail itself (each machine reads it from the server), window size, layout, zoom, collapsed folders, your filing habits, the interface language.
Setup

Settings → P2P sync: turn it on and enter the SAME pairing code (12 characters minimum; “Generate” suggests one) on every machine. An older, shorter code turns sync off: generate a new one. The machines must be on the same network (or enter a machine's IP address in “Static peers” — useful through a VPN), with their clocks set correctly (the most recent change wins). Ports: UDP 54321 (discovery) and TCP 54322 (exchange) to allow in a firewall.
The ⇄ indicator and diagnostics

The indicator at the bottom of the side panel shows the state (“1 peer(s)”, “synced at 14:32”, “no machine seen”…). The sync page shows network diagnostics: addresses, listening ports, announcements sent / received, machines running another version, code too short. “Search for machines” probes the local network if automatic discovery is blocked (router, VPN, guest Wi-Fi). All machines must run the same version of MintMail.
Sync security

The channel is encrypted and authenticated by the pairing code; passwords never travel in clear; received data is strictly validated before being applied. Keep the code secret: anyone who knows it and shares your network can pair.

sections.title: Offline and reliability
items: Offline mode

If the network goes down, your actions (move, archive, delete, mark read, favorite) stay instant in the interface and are recorded: they are replayed in order as soon as the network is back. The status message reads “Offline — N action(s) waiting”. A definitive refusal from the server drops the action with a clear message (never an infinite loop).
Messages are never lost

A message whose sending fails because of the network is kept and retried automatically (every minute, up to 10 times). A refusal from the server (address refused, credentials…) comes back to you with “Reopen” so you can fix it. Scheduled messages also go out with the window closed (see “Undo send and scheduled send”).
Real-time reception
MintMail uses IMAP IDLE: new messages arrive within seconds, with a desktop notification (can be turned off). A full refresh happens every N minutes (Appearance, 1 to 60) or on demand (Ctrl+R).
Performance

Persistent IMAP connections, progressive loading, list updated without rebuilding, bulk actions in a single transaction: archiving or marking a sender as spam takes a few milliseconds in the interface, the server follows in the background.

sections.title: Appearance and settings
items: Styles and theme

Settings → Appearance: three styles — Aurora (bright dark, default), Paper (warm light), Terminal (green on black) — each in light or dark (or following the system), accent color, list density (compact, comfortable, airy), message text zoom. ☰ → “Switch light / dark” to change in one click.
Other settings

• Load remote images (not recommended) · desktop notifications · refresh frequency · undo-send delay · interface language (restart required). Languages: French, English, Dutch, German, Spanish — the last three are AI translations not reviewed by native speakers, and the F1 help stays in English for them.
• Gestures & layout: layout, swipe gestures, touchpad reversal, conversations.
• Settings → Shortcuts: list of keys. “Reset appearance” restores the defaults.
Settings pages

Accounts · Signatures · Appearance · ✨ Artificial intelligence · P2P sync · Gestures & layout · Filters & blocking · Reply templates · Contacts · Sending identities · Calendar (Google / CalDAV) · Shortcuts · Updates · Help & Credits. Esc goes back to the inbox.

sections.title: Automatic updates
items: How it works

MintMail looks for a new version on GitHub (repository set in Settings → Updates) at most ONCE A DAY and tells you about it. Only one anonymous request is sent, with no personal data. Can be turned off in Settings → Updates; palette → “Check for updates” to check right away. When a version is available, a BANNER appears at the top of the window as soon as it opens (“Install now”, “Release notes”, “Later”) and a “⬆ Update X” chip stays in the side panel. “Later” hides the banner for 24 h for that version; ✕ hides it until the next launch. If the window is not in the foreground, a desktop notification also announces the new version (once). If the update is already installed, the banner simply offers “Restart now”. “mintmail --check-update” gives the details in a terminal.
Install in one click

Settings → Updates → “Install the update” (or “Install now” in the banner): the package is downloaded with a progress bar, its signature is checked, then the system asks for your administrator password. The banner then switches to “installed” with a “Restart now” button. Nothing is installed without your approval.
Update security

• Every version is signed by SAEC. The verification key is installed with MintMail (/usr/share/mintmail/update-pubkey.pem, owned by root): no setting, no “Release” and no hacked GitHub account can replace it. GitHub is only the transport.
• Refused: missing or invalid signature, a package that is not MintMail, a version that is not strictly newer (no going back), a corrupted or oversized download, an unexpected host.
• The program that installs runs as administrator, copies the package into a private folder, re-checks everything on that copy, then installs with apt.
• Without an installed verification key, MintMail only INFORMS you about new versions.
If automatic installation is disabled

The Updates page gives the reason. Verification key missing: this MintMail was not built by the signed release chain. pkexec missing: sudo apt install policykit-1. In every case you can download the .deb from the GitHub “Release” and run: sudo apt install ./mintmail_X.Y.Z_all.deb.
Publish a version (developers)
See docs/RELEASING.md in the repository: a single version number (VERSION file), CHANGELOG.md journal, vX.Y.Z tag, package signed by tools/release.sh.

sections.title: Security and privacy
items: Where your data is

• Settings: {config}/config.json (passwords and keys in the system keyring when it is available).
• Message cache: {data}/cache.db · Log: {log} · Diagnostic report: {data}/diagnostic.txt.
• Mail stays on your server; the local cache is a copy. Deleting an account erases its cache, not your mail.
What protects you

• Encrypted (TLS) IMAP/SMTP connections with certificate verification; passwordless OAuth for Gmail and Outlook.
• Received mail: the HTML is rebuilt from an allow-list (scripts, forms, frames, redirects and dangerous styles removed) and shown under a content security policy; remote images blocked by default; JavaScript disabled; no cookie or cache kept.
• Links: only http, https and mailto open (never file:, javascript:, smb:, ssh:…). Attachments: programs and scripts (.exe, .sh, .desktop, .AppImage…) are never opened from MintMail (save only); risky files (HTML, SVG, Office macros…) ask for confirmation.
• Your data: MintMail's folders are 0700 and files 0600 (mail, attachments, settings, log: unreadable by the machine's other accounts).
• Encrypted and authenticated sync, limited to the local network; weak codes refused; unsubscribe and CalDAV over HTTPS, with no request to your internal network.
• AI: text is sent only if you turn it on, never with Ollama, no action without approval; a booby-trapped message can still fool a model (distorted summary or sorting): check before approving.
• Known limits and the audit report: the SECURITY.md file (project repository and /usr/share/doc/mintmail/).
Report a security flaw

Write to contact@saec.me describing the problem and how to reproduce it. Please do not publish it before it is fixed. A fixed version will be released as soon as possible; only the latest version is maintained.
Error log
☰ → Error log shows the latest incidents. If there is a problem at startup, MintMail shows a clear message and offers to set settings and cache aside (nothing is deleted).

sections.title: Command line and troubleshooting
items: Options of the mintmail command
@CLI@
MintMail does not start

1. Run “/usr/bin/mintmail” in a terminal: the message gives the cause.
2. “/usr/bin/mintmail --diagnose”: full report (copy it if you ask for help).
3. Missing component: sudo apt install python3-gi gir1.2-gtk-3.0 gir1.2-webkit2-4.1.
4. Damaged data: “mintmail --reset” (backs up, then starts clean; accounts come back by themselves if sync is on).
MintMail always uses /usr/bin/python3: another Python (conda, pyenv…) does not get in the way.
An old version opens / wrong icon

An old local installation (~/.local, /usr/local, /opt folder) can hide the package: “/usr/bin/mintmail --remove-local-install” lists it, then “--yes” sets it aside. The taskbar icon updates after you close and reopen your session.
The machines do not see each other (sync)

Check in Settings → P2P sync: the SAME code (12 characters minimum) everywhere, the same MintMail version, the same network, UDP 54321 / TCP 54322 ports open. Try “Search for machines”, or enter the other machine's IP in “Static peers”.
Gmail / Outlook refuses the connection

With a password: use an app password (Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud) and enable IMAP access on the account. Without a password: “OAuth” provider (see “Google / Microsoft sign-in”). Google in testing mode: add your address to the test users.
The AI does not answer

Settings → AI → “Test the connection” gives the cause. Invalid key or quota exceeded (NVIDIA); Ollama not running or model missing (“ollama serve”, “ollama pull …”); address without https:// for a remote service.
Update and uninstall

Update: sudo apt install ./mintmail_X.Y.Z_all.deb (your settings and cache are kept). Uninstall: sudo apt remove mintmail (add purge to also remove the package files; your personal data stays in {config} and {data} until you delete it).

welcome: A fast, polished mail client for Linux Mint, with a discreet AI that saves you time. Your mail, your keys and your settings stay with you.
steps: Settings (Ctrl+,) → Accounts → “＋ Add an account”. Gmail and Outlook: OAuth sign-in, no password.
Click a message to read it; E archives, S stars, P pins, T opens “Today”.
Turn on the AI, if you like
Settings → ✨ Artificial intelligence: summaries, drafts, assistant (Ctrl+J), sorting. Entirely optional.
Find everything on your other computers
Settings → P2P sync: accounts, signatures and settings follow you from one computer to the next.
tips: Ctrl+K opens the command palette: almost every action is there, just type a few letters.
T opens “Today”: your calendar, priorities and tasks on a single page.
Start a search with ? to ask the AI a question, for example “? March invoices”.
H snoozes the message until tomorrow 8 am.
X turns on selection mode: tick several messages, then archive, delete or sort them in one go.
J and K move to the next or previous message without leaving the keyboard.
\\ switches between columns and list only: handy on a small screen.
P pins a message; on servers that accept it, the pin follows you to your other computers.
Settings → Appearance: pick Aurora, Paper or Terminal, light or dark.
“mintmail --check-update”, in a terminal, tells you whether a new version is waiting.
When a new version exists, a banner appears at every launch; “Later” hides it for 24 h.
F1 opens this help at any time; the search accepts a word or part of a word, accents optional.
